intent: Reduce Cinnamon X11 background memory by running a Qt Core resident with native XCB listeners and StatusNotifier/dbusmenu tray, while launching a bounded ephemeral GUI process for capture. Preserve legacy graphical paths, accepted capture target identity, source privacy, cancellation, durable artifact/clipboard behavior, UI activation and existing IPC/storage contracts. This is an incremental memory candidate, not a complete-product release.

findings.suggested_fix: Prepare and fill the private unlinked spool in a bounded worker, then commit XCB ownership on the session thread only after verifying both clipboard revision and copy-eligibility generation again. Preserve old ownership on worker error, keep a finite single-write admission bound and release worker payload promptly. Propagate invalidation through SourceAdapter so a newer action cannot be overwritten by stale asynchronous completion.
findings.title: Clipboard spooling blocks the resident event loop
findings.why_it_matters: Copying a local-only image/text result performs the entire private spool write and flush synchronously on the resident QObject thread. A large accepted image or slow/full temporary filesystem can stall hotkeys, tray events, IPC and cancellation while ownership is prepared, violating the R20 responsiveness contract. The earlier worker reads/verifies the artifact but returns before this new disk write happens.
findings.validation_reason: At b6e987c, a saved single detached local-only image/text result reaches OperationService.cpp:297–300 through the resident-thread queued completion at line 65 and synchronous adapter copy at X11CoreSourceAdapter.cpp:22, so the newly introduced full write/flush at X11Clipboard.cpp:191 can block resident event handling for a large result or slow temporary filesystem contrary to R20; incidence and stall duration were not measured live.
